title: URL Slug Generator: SEO-Friendly Slugs
description: Turn titles into clean, lowercase URL slugs: accents removed, spaces and punctuation become hyphens, with stop-word removal, max length and bulk mode.
quickAnswer: A URL slug is the readable part of a web address that identifies a page, such as percentage-change-calculator. To make one, lowercase the title, remove accents, replace spaces and punctuation with hyphens and trim the ends: 'Héllo, Wörld! 2026' becomes hello-world-2026. Keep slugs short and descriptive, and do not change them once a page is published.

formula.title: How a Slug Is Built
formula.expression: Title → NFD normalise and remove accents → lowercase → non-letters and non-digits become the separator → collapse repeats → trim the ends
formula.explanation: Unicode NFD normalisation splits letters such as é into e plus an accent mark, and the marks are removed. Letters that do not split (ß, æ, ø, ł) are written out as ss, ae, o and l, and & becomes 'and'. Everything that is not a letter or a digit becomes a single separator, and separators at the start or end are removed. Optional steps drop common English stop words and cut the slug at a word boundary so it stays within a maximum length. Letters from non-Latin scripts are kept, because browsers display them, but you may prefer to translate the title first.

variables.name: Separator
variables.description: Hyphens (-) are the usual choice for URLs; underscores (_) suit file names and some systems.

variables.name: Stop words
variables.description: Short words such as a, the, and, of, to that rarely help a URL. At least one word is always kept.

variables.name: Max length
variables.description: Cuts the slug before the word that would go over the limit, so words are never chopped in half.

commonMistakes.title: Changing the slug of a live page
commonMistakes.description: A new slug is a new URL. Links, bookmarks and search results that point to the old address break unless you set up a permanent (301) redirect. Choose the slug carefully before publishing.

commonMistakes.title: Stuffing keywords into the slug
commonMistakes.description: best-cheap-free-calculator-online-calculator-tool reads as spam. A short, accurate slug that matches the page title is easier to read and share.

commonMistakes.title: Using dates that will go out of date
commonMistakes.description: A slug like best-laptops-2024 looks stale the following year, and changing it later means a redirect. Leave dates out unless the page is about a specific year.

commonMistakes.title: Mixing upper and lower case
commonMistakes.description: Paths on many servers are case-sensitive, so /About-Us and /about-us can be different pages. Lowercase slugs avoid duplicate URLs.

commonMistakes.title: Using underscores in web addresses
commonMistakes.description: Google's guidance recommends hyphens to separate words in URLs; words joined by underscores can be read as a single word.

howto.name: How to Create a URL Slug
howto.description: Turn a page title into a clean, SEO-friendly URL slug.

steps.name: Type the title
steps.text: Enter the page or post title, or switch to Bulk mode and paste one title per line.

steps.name: Choose the options
steps.text: Pick hyphens or underscores, and optionally remove stop words or set a maximum length.

steps.name: Copy the slug
steps.text: Copy the slug and use it as the last part of the page's URL.

faqs.a: It is the part of a web address that names a specific page, usually after the last slash. In toolsbuilt.com/tools/slug-generator/ the slug is slug-generator.

faqs.q: Should I use hyphens or underscores in URLs?
faqs.a: Use hyphens. Google recommends hyphens to separate words in URLs, and they are the common convention. Underscores are fine for file names.

faqs.q: Should I remove stop words like 'the' and 'and' from slugs?
faqs.a: Often, yes, when it makes the slug shorter without losing meaning, such as write-best-guide instead of how-to-write-the-best-guide. Keep them if the slug reads badly without them.

faqs.q: How long should a URL slug be?
faqs.a: There is no fixed limit, but three to five meaningful words is a good target. Use the max length option to keep slugs within a limit without cutting words.

faqs.q: How are accents and special characters handled?
faqs.a: Accents are removed with Unicode normalisation, so é becomes e and ü becomes u; ß becomes ss, and & becomes 'and'. Other symbols turn into the separator.

faqs.q: Can I make slugs for many titles at once?
faqs.a: Yes. Use Bulk mode and paste one title per line. Turn on unique numbering to add -2, -3 and so on to repeated slugs.

faqs.q: Does changing a slug affect SEO?
faqs.a: Changing the URL of an existing page means search engines must find the new address. Use a 301 redirect from the old slug so links and rankings carry over.

slug-checklist.heading: Slug Checklist
slug-checklist.li1: Short and descriptive: a reader should guess what the page is about from the URL alone.
slug-checklist.li2: Lowercase with hyphens: consistent, easy to type and recommended by Google.
slug-checklist.li3: No dates or numbers that will change: unless they are part of what the page is.
slug-checklist.li4: Stable: once published, keep the slug. If you must change it, redirect the old URL permanently.
slug-checklist.li5: Unique: two pages in the same folder cannot share a slug; bulk mode numbers repeats for you.
slug-checklist.p1: ToolsBuilt follows these rules for its own pages, such as /tools/remove-duplicate-lines/ and /tools/text-diff-checker/. Everything on this page runs in your browser and nothing you type is stored.
